basis: Microcephaly, intellectual disability and young-onset diabetes define the syndrome; hearing and dental abnormalities occur in under 30%.
Endogenous ethanol production defines an acquired metabolic disorder; fermentation sites do not establish local injury, and intoxication is transient.
Squamous carcinoma originates in scrotal skin; its reproductive-region location does not change the cutaneous origin.
Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia defines the disease; neurodevelopmental abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting neurologic injury beyond transient hypoglycemic symptoms.
Agnosia causes loss of higher-order recognition of emotional expressions and nonverbal signals; this is neurologic perceptual dysfunction.
Impaired limb perfusion defines a vascular disorder; muscle necrosis, neuropathy and skin loss are not established across the concept.
Skin, ocular and brain anomalies define the syndrome; acral malformations are also a defining skeletal feature, although frequencies are unavailable.
Pseudocowpox is a localized parapoxvirus infection producing characteristic cutaneous nodules.
Clostridial infection causes defining skeletal-muscle necrosis with destructive skin and soft-tissue involvement.
Hereditary protein-deposition disorder; renal amyloid 3/3, cardiac amyloid 4/4 with heart failure, hepatic amyloid 3/3 with failure; cutaneous findings omitted at cap.
Primary ovarian insufficiency includes gonadal endocrine failure, supported by elevated FSH and decreased AMH in 2/2 patients.
Seckel skeletal dwarfism/microcephaly with insulin resistance and hypertriglyceridemia; hepatic steatosis 2/2; retinal detachment 1/2 omitted at cap.
A focal epilepsy syndrome; its benign and transitory course does not alter its neurologic classification.
Umbrella malignancy of bone and mesenchymal soft tissues, including muscle, cartilage and fibrous tissue; individual visceral sites do not define the group.
Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia is a lymphoplasmacytic B-cell lymphoma involving marrow and monoclonal immunoglobulin production.
Glycosylation disorder with immune dysfunction; neurodevelopmental deficits 1/1 and anemia 2/2; ocular, joint, vascular and hepatic findings omitted at cap.
Thrombosis occupies intracranial blood vessels; brain infarction is a possible consequence, with insufficient evidence that parenchymal injury meets the threshold.
Congenital enlargement of toes is a structural limb and skeletal abnormality.
Tumor arises from CNS glial cells; mixed cellular differentiation does not establish another organ of origin.
Tumor originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; neural differentiation does not establish nervous-system involvement.
Nocardia bacterial infection; pulmonary infection with pneumonia occurs in 30-79%. CNS, cutaneous and hepatic infections are occasional, below 30%.
Benign tumor originates in the parathyroid endocrine gland; hyperparathyroidism and its organ complications are not established by this concept.
Fibrosis affects mammary parenchyma; breast disease has no axis, and this is not a cutaneous fibrosing disorder.
Fallopian-tube diverticulosis causes nodular thickening at a reproductive site; the definition does not establish infection or immune-mediated disease.
Diffuse inflammation of the corneal stroma defines ocular disease; a specific infectious or immune-mediated etiology is not established.
